text:
anya: Quick sync — I'm drafting the PRD + RFC for the kernel catalog + KV cache policy changes customers asked for. Need scope decisions: shipping minimal set vs broader opt-in rollout. TL;DR: customers want lower-cost quantized kernels + smarter KV fallback for long-contexts.

jamal: Can you paste the rough acceptance criteria you have so far? will help us scope engineering work.

anya: Sure — early draft: 1) Kernel catalog API that maps model -> kernel variant (float32, int8, int4) 2) KV cache policy that prefers prefix/KV caching for repeated prefixes and falls back to streaming for novel tokens 3) Canary rollout path + automatic fallback on regressions 4) Cost/latency metric targets: p50 token latency no worse than baseline+10ms, cost per token reduced by >=15% on quantized paths.

li: For Dedicated/Private we need to ensure customers can pin kernels. Also need a feature flag at the node-agent level to opt in/out per deployment.

marco: We must include model-level quality checks — hallucination/regression tests. Quantization sometimes changes logits ordering on rare tokens. Propose a canary eval set parity check with threshold: LM-EMBED/QA F1 drop <1.5%.

jamal: From runtime side: big questions: automatic kernel selection heuristic (latency-first vs cost-first), and how KV cache interacts with kernel switch (cache format compatibility). If switching kernel invalidates KV format we need migration plan.

anya: Scope negotiation: Option A (MVP): expose kernel preferences in catalog, implement a safe quantized kernel for GPT-like decoders with explicit compatibility guarantee; KV policy v1: prefix cache + simple LRU eviction, no cross-kernel migration. Option B (expanded): add automatic routing by request latency budget, cross-kernel KV migration, per-customer rollout console. Which do we prefer?

oliver: Product POV: many customers will accept Option A if we make the rollback instant and document limitations. Option B is nicer but doubles implementation time. We should aim for A with clear signal hooks and a roadmap item to B.

sara: SRE notes: Need observability hooks: per-request kernel id, cache hit/miss, cache-key-ttl, and a 5-min fallback histogram. Also, alerting rules: if p95 token latency increases >20% after canary, auto rollback.

nina: QA: Test plan items: unit tests for kernel selection, integration test where same prompt runs on all kernels and diff is computed, end-to-end canary with synthetic traffic, perf runs on representative sequence-length distribution. We'll need labelled prompt sets for regression detection.

marco: Edge cases: 1) extremely long KV chains where quantized kernels drop precision, 2) streaming responses where mid-stream kernel change happens, 3) multi-turn chat where cache contains mixed-kernel entries. Suggest we disallow mid-request kernel swaps and mark cache entries with kernel-version tag.

jamal: Implementation notes: kernel-catalog table fields: model_name, kernel_id, kernel_type, quantized_bits, compatibility_tags. API PATCH to update mapping. KV entries: {key, value, kernel_tag, seq_len}. We'll add simple migration: on read, if kernel_tag != current_kernel and fallback_allowed -> treat as miss and recompute.

anya: Acceptance checklist (for PRD/RFC):
- [ ] Kernel catalog API spec + openapi schema
- [ ] Runtime: safe quantized kernel implement + unit tests
- [ ] KV v1: prefix cache + per-entry kernel_tag and LRU eviction
- [ ] Canary plan + automated rollback hooks (alerts + deploy-bot integration)
- [ ] Regression eval suite & threshold definitions
- [ ] Docs for Dedicated/Private pinning behavior
- [ ] Performance targets: p50 latency <= baseline+10ms, cost/token >=15% improvement on targeted workloads

oliver: Also add acceptance: 'no customer-facing API changes that require client code updates' unless explicitly documented.

jamal: Timeline ask: if we scope to Option A, eng estimates 6 weeks (2w infra/catalog + 3w kernel + 1w QA/canary). Option B is +6-8 weeks.

anya: Thanks — next steps: I'll update RFC with Option A as default, include the checklist above, and tag owners. Please react with :thumbsup: if you agree to Option A + backlogged Option B.

jamal: :thumbsup:
marco: :thumbsup:
li: :thumbsup:
ns (typo) -> sara: :thumbsup:
ng: nina: :thumbsup:

anya: I'll post the RFC link in #eng-releases after I finish the initial draft. If anyone has explicit customer asks that require Option B now, ping me directly.
